title: Echarse a: Bursting Into an Action

sections.content:
You know *empezar a* + infinitive from A2 Unit 28 and *ponerse a* + infinitive from A2 Unit 32. *Echarse a* + infinitive also means "to start doing something", but only when the start is a sudden reaction: nobody plans it, it just bursts out. It is used mainly with a few verbs of feeling and movement, such as *llorar* (to cry), *reír* (to laugh) and *correr* (to run).

*Echarse* is reflexive, so the pronoun and the verb change with the subject (*me eché*, *se echó*, *nos echamos*). The infinitive after *a* never changes.

sections.title: echarse a + infinitive
rows: Al oír la noticia, se echó a llorar.
On hearing the news, she burst into tears.
Todos nos echamos a reír al mismo tiempo.
We all burst out laughing at the same time.
Cuando vio al perro, el niño se echó a correr.
When he saw the dog, the boy broke into a run.
Los caballos se echaron a correr por el campo.
The horses broke into a run across the field.

sections.content: Use *echarse a* only for a sudden reaction. A planned task needs *ponerse a* or *empezar a*: *Se puso a estudiar* is natural, *Se echó a estudiar* is not. A reaction can use either verb (*se echó a llorar* and *se puso a llorar* are both correct), but *echarse a* sounds more sudden.
